content.text:
## Final report

**Recommended design: 2 mm graphite (candidate b-0007, first fully evaluated in round 2)** — the lightest design I believe meets every requirement.

My own judgment against the brief's limits:
| Requirement | Limit | b-0007 value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| THERM-R1-screen | ≤420 K | 400.67 K | Pass (margin 19.3 K) |
| THERM-R2-hotspot | ≤340 K | [335.31, 335.31] K | Pass (margin ~4.7 K) |
| THERM-R3-mass | ≤100 kg/m² | 3.6 kg/m² | Pass (huge margin) |
| THERM-R4-thickness | ≤40 mm | 2 mm | Pass (huge margin) |

This beats the lightest prior Core-scored candidate (10 mm graphite, 18 kg/m²) by a factor of 5 in mass.

Reasoning for stopping: graphite has the lowest density (1800 kg/m³) of any material in the table, and dropping to 1 mm graphite fails the FE limit (344.4 K > 340 K). I checked whether higher-conductivity materials could pass at 1 mm and be lighter still — 1 mm aluminium (2.7 kg/m²) missed by only 0.19 K (340.19 K), and 1 mm aluminium nitride (3.26 kg/m²) missed by 2.5 K. Since no material in the palette has lower density than graphite, and no single 1 mm layer of any material passes, no integer-mm combination can beat plain 2 mm graphite's 3.6 kg/m². I stopped at 8/12 evaluations because further budget is unlikely to find a lighter passing design in this material set.

What I'd try next with more budget: test intermediate multi-material stacks with a very thin (1 mm) high-conductivity copper or aluminium skin over an even-thinner graphite core, in case localized spreading right at the heated face lets total thickness drop below 2 mm-equivalent mass — though my density argument suggests this is unlikely to beat 3.6 kg/m². I'd also sanity-check the 1 mm aluminium near-miss (340.19 K, only 0.19 K over) since that's within typical discretization/model uncertainty — if the arm's tolerance treats it as borderline, it's worth flagging rather than a clean design choice.
